logic.note: Runs the real compiled firmware on an ATmega328P emulator (avr8js): GPIO, timers, USART, ADC, watchdog, interrupts, SPI and TWI (I2C, master mode) behave like the chip; Wire and SPI talk to the I2C and SPI parts wired to SDA/SCL (A4/A5) and MOSI/MISO/SCK (D11/D12/D13).

timing.note: Cycle-counted at 16 MHz on a deterministic virtual clock, so delay()/millis() are exact in virtual time. Peripherals the emulator lacks (e.g. some timer modes, sleep) and the crystal's ±50 ppm drift are not modelled.

analog.note: Pins are ideal sources with 25 Ω output resistance. Digital inputs use the datasheet thresholds (low ≤ 0.3·VCC, high ≥ 0.6·VCC) and keep their last level in between. The ADC reads the solved net voltage against a 5 V reference; AREF, noise and input capacitance are ignored.

power.note: Round 6: USB (power.usb, default plugged) is a stiff 5 V source on 5V; VIN goes through a 5 V regulator (~1.1 V dropout) and 3.3 V comes from 5 V through an LDO; with USB unplugged and nothing on VIN / 5V the firmware is held in reset (below 4 V on 5V). Per-pin current above 40 mA is flagged; total-package (200 mA) and regulator limits, the USB / VIN auto-switch and a gradual brownout are not simulated.

emulates: ATmega328P CPU at 16 MHz via avr8js
Same pin map as the Uno
On-board L LED on D13 and ON LED
doesNotEmulate: RESET pin and the reset button
VIN, barrel jack and regulator limits
Target (slave) mode of the two-wire interface, Wire.begin(address): the board can only be the bus master
Two-wire bus electrical detail: the bus carries whole bytes, not SDA/SCL edges, so clock stretching, rise times and bus capacitance are not modelled
Floating inputs: an input with nothing driving it reads LOW instead of random noise (the simulator warns about it)
testOnRealDevice: Total current from many pins (200 mA package limit)
Anything powered from VIN or the 3.3 V pin (50 mA max)
Analog readings near the input thresholds
